channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Portugal’s Housing Protest Draws Thousands After Police Clashes
item.description: Thousands of people took to the streets of Portugal’s second-largest city Thursday to protest against the country’s soaring home prices after the police clashed with demonstrators in the early morning hours, increasing pressure on the government to act.
item.dc:creator: Henrique Almeida

item.title: Zelenskyy: ‘Pity’ Ukraine Losing Strong Partner
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Marc Short, former Chief of Staff to former Vice President Mike Pence, says reports of graft and corruption involving the Trump administration and the president's family are becoming a bigger liability for Republicans ahead of the midterms. Rep. Gabe Amo (D-RI), Vice Ranking Member on Foreign Affairs Committee, says the Trump administration should act against Russia and argues it has repeatedly failed to clearly stand with Ukraine. Heather Conley, senior fellow at AEI, a senior advisor at Evenflow Macro LLC and former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, says Russian President Vladimir Putin sees an opportunity to intensify pressure on Ukraine as questions grow over US intelligence sharing, Starshield access and Washington's commitment to Kyiv. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore’s Wong Says Probing Firms Behind Haze-Causing Fires
item.description: Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong vowed to identify companies that may be responsible for the fires shrouding the city-state in haze for weeks, warning that those found culpable could face legal action.
item.dc:creator: Cindy Wang

item.title: Conley Says Putin Is Testing NATO Unity
item.description: Heather Conley, senior fellow at AEI, a senior advisor at Evenflow Macro LLC and former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, says Russian President Vladimir Putin sees an opportunity to intensify pressure on Ukraine as questions grow over US intelligence sharing, Starshield access and Washington's commitment to Kyiv. Conley says Russian attacks are increasingly threatening Ukraine's economy and approaching NATO territory, arguing Putin is probing whether he can break the alliance's unity amid uncertainty over US support. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Amo Says Trump Should Enforce Russia Sanctions
item.description: Rep. Gabe Amo (D-RI), Vice Ranking Member on Foreign Affairs Committee, says the Trump administration should act against Russia and argues it has repeatedly failed to clearly stand with Ukraine. Rep. Amo says Congress needs to determine whether changes to Starshield capabilities or intelligence sharing impeded Ukraine's defense and says lawmakers should use Congress's power of the purse to demand answers and accountability. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Andreessen Rises as a MAGA Power Player
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Through PACs and funding tied to a16z's co-founders and partners, the Andreessen Horowitz team has poured at least $116 million into federal politics since Trump's reelection. Andreessen, who voted for Hillary Clinton in 2016 and said back then that Trump’s immigration regime “makes me sick to my stomach,” explained on a podcast that he was compelled by “absolutely horrifying” discussions he once had with Biden officials. In his retelling, they divulged a top-secret plan for the federal government to take control of the AI industry and outlaw all startups and open-source software.
Austin Carr, Bloomberg News Senior Features Writer Ed Ludlow, Host of Bloomberg Tech Robert Schiffman, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Tech Credit Analyst Angela Stent, Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Short: Corruption Is Growing Liability for Republicans
item.description: Marc Short, former Chief of Staff to former Vice President Mike Pence, says reports of graft and corruption involving the Trump administration and the president's family are becoming a bigger liability for Republicans ahead of the midterms. Short says Republicans need a stronger closing message to motivate voters and argues that Trump's turn toward Russian President Vladimir Putin, including Russian diesel imports, is economically senseless and "dead wrong." He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Musk Pours $158 Million Into GOP Super PAC for Texas Senate Race
item.description: Elon Musk gave $158 million to the GOP’s main super PAC backing Senate candidates in September, making the world’s richest person the biggest US political donor for the second straight election cycle, according to the latest filings from the Federal Election Commission.
item.dc:creator: Bill Allison and Dana Hull

item.title: US Says Trump Did Not Restrict Ukraine's Access to SpaceX Defense Tech
item.description: A senior US official said President Donald Trump didn’t limit Ukraine’s access to SpaceX’s Starshield satellite technology. The system is used to knock down Russian drones. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Trump restricted the access. Bloomberg's Kate Sullivan reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Seeks Culprits as Texas Senate Seat, Others Are in Peril
item.description: President Donald Trump railed at Senator John Cornyn of Texas and longtime GOP strategist Karl Rove, accusing them of undermining Ken Paxton’s Senate campaign in the state, a crucial contest for Republican hopes of retaining control of the chamber.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Bolsonaro, Lula in Tight Race Ahead of Brazil Runoff, Poll Shows
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva are locked in a close race ahead of Brazil’s runoff election, according to a new poll.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati

item.title: Kansas Senate Race Turns Into Tossup, Sabato Says
item.description: The US Senate race in Kansas has turned into a tossup according to pollster Larry Sabato. Polls show incumbent Republican Roger Marshall and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton are neck-and-neck. A Democrat hasn't won this seat in almost 100 years. Bloomberg's Amanda Albright reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Treasuries Soar as Tech Slump Threatens Growth
item.description: Treasuries led a global bond rally as a selloff in artificial-intelligence shares deepened, spurring demand for havens from a growth slowdown. A measure of CoreWeave’s credit risk climbed to an all-time high Thursday as its high-yield bonds extended declines. We get reaction from Bloomberg Tech host Ed Ludlow. Steve Kaplan of JPMorgan Asset Management joins to discuss trends in portfolio diversification. Bloomberg's Austin Carr examines Marc Andreessen's rise as a MAGA power player ahead of midterms. Plus - US producer prices rose in September at the fastest pace in more than four years as higher energy costs reverberated through the US economy. We examine what it could mean for monetary policy with Frank Monkam, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Reckons With a World Where Trump Is Now Helping Putin
item.description: European leaders know they can’t stop courting Donald Trump. But as the US president menaces Ukraine and offers Russian an economic lifeline, they are preparing for a world where he effectively sides with Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano, Alberto Nardelli and Ott Tammik

item.title: Big AI Is Pouring Millions Into the Midterms
item.description: AI is a major force in the 2026 US midterms, with industry groups spending hundreds of millions of dollars to elect candidates who might write the rules governing the controversial technology. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Outage Revives Concerns Over Relying on Musk’s SpaceX
item.description: In 2024, US lawmakers from both parties worried if the billionaire would cut off access over Taiwan.
item.dc:creator: Ted Mann

item.title: Trump Didn’t Order Limits on Kyiv’s SpaceX Access, US Says
item.description: President Donald Trump didn’t order any limitations on Ukraine’s access to SpaceX’s Starshield satellite technology, according to a senior US official.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan, Ellen Milligan and Sana Pashankar

item.title: Musk Post Sows Confusion Over Ukraine Starshield Disruption
item.description: Hours after Ukrainian officials discovered a restriction on Starlink terminals that disrupted the country’s military operations, SpaceX Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk sought to shift responsibility away from his company.
item.dc:creator: Sana Pashankar

item.title: US Ties With South Korea Hit Low Point Over Intelligence Row
item.description: South Korea’s longstanding alliance with America is being tested by spats spanning from investment deals to intelligence leaks, compromising Seoul’s ability to respond to North Korea.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Trump Rejects Hegseth’s Bid to Stream Firing Squad Execution
item.description: President Donald Trump rejected plans to livestream the execution of a former Army major who killed 13 people in 2009, overruling Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s proposal after facing intense bipartisan backlash.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason
